routes.description: Establish God as the better explanation of natural order, rational norms, moral obligation, purpose, and the central claims of Christian experience.
routes.successCriteria: Show that these features of reality are more adequately grounded in an eternal personal mind than in an exclusively natural reality.

motionBridge.description: Connect the combined explanatory case for a transcendent personal mind to the conclusion that God exists.

centralBridges.description: Show that cosmic order, origins, fine-tuning, or biological information warrant an inference to intelligence.
Show that mind-independent logic and mathematical intelligibility require grounding in a transcendent mind.
Show that objective human value and binding moral duties require a personal standard beyond society.
Connect the historical and self-sacrificial account of Jesus to the character of the proposed God.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Defend abductive inference to intelligent causes as legitimate rather than excluded by methodological assumptions.
Explain how relationship with God supplies purpose and reasons for costly service to other people.

routes.description: Withhold belief in God by requiring publicly testable support and explaining the cited natural, rational, moral, and experiential phenomena without deity.
routes.successCriteria: Show that the affirmative inferences do not demonstrate God because natural accounts remain available and religious claims lack reliable verification.

motionBridge.description: Connect the failure of the offered evidence to satisfy the affirmative burden with nonacceptance of God's existence.

centralBridges.description: Require testable, publicly verifiable evidence capable of distinguishing a real deity from unsupported religious claims.
Show that natural inquiry and uncertain origin models do not require a supernatural designer.
Explain logical and mathematical relations through the properties of things without invoking a divine mind.
Ground moral judgment and cooperation in harm, empathy, trust, and social dependence without divine command.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Show that conflicting and psychologically fallible religious experiences cannot identify a uniquely true religion.
Keep the burden on the party asserting an additional supernatural reality rather than demanding its disproof.

sectionSelections.title: Evidence, Method, and the Burden of Belief
sectionSelections.rationale: The governing standard of evidence determines whether design and religious claims can support the motion and who must establish an additional supernatural reality.

proSelections.proposition: Methodological naturalism can exclude intelligent causes in advance, whereas abductive historical reasoning permits an inference from effects to immaterial intelligence.

conSelections.proposition: Incompatible and untestable religious convictions do not constitute knowledge, and no physical or logical evidence identifies a god.
Methodological naturalism keeps inquiry directed toward factual explanations, while invoking God supplies neither a testable mechanism nor an explanation.

sectionSelections.title: Design, Biological Complexity, and Cosmic Origins
sectionSelections.rationale: The inference from natural structure and origins to intelligence is a direct route to God's existence and a principal point of dispute between the sides.

proSelections.proposition: Fine-tuned physical laws and the information-rich complexity of living cells are unexpected on materialism and therefore support a designer.
Evolution does not explain cosmic origins, and ordinary causal reasoning makes an originating cause or mind behind the universe more probable.

conSelections.proposition: Biochemical complexity is haphazard and inefficient rather than indicative of intelligent design, and proposed irreducible-complexity cases have been refuted.
Atheism need not assert that the universe came from nothing because cosmological origins remain uncertain and some models include an eternal singularity.

sectionSelections.title: Logic, Mathematics, and Intelligibility
sectionSelections.rationale: Whether objective rational relations require a mind is an independent bridge from the intelligibility of reality to a transcendent personal source.

proSelections.proposition: Objective mathematical and logical truths exist independently of human minds and are best grounded in the nature of a personal divine mind.

conSelections.proposition: Mathematical relations follow from the properties of whatever exists and do not require a deity to decree or sustain them.

sectionSelections.title: Morality, Altruism, and Human Purpose
sectionSelections.rationale: The debate's moral route turns on whether objective duties and costly altruism require divine grounding or can arise from human social and moral capacities.

proSelections.proposition: Objective human value, moral duties, and moral progress require a mind beyond humanity rather than value assigned by human beings alone.
Theistic and atheistic worldviews should be compared by their ability to justify altruism, human rights, and costly personal sacrifice.

conSelections.proposition: Morality arises through social trust, empathy, cooperation, and selection against harmful selfishness rather than from the Christian God.
Morality rests on the understood wrongness of unnecessary harm, while political and religious dogmas provide excuses for violating that standard.

sectionSelections.title: Christian Claims and Religious Experience
sectionSelections.rationale: The motion also depends on whether specifically Christian claims and personal experience reliably identify God rather than culturally variable or psychological belief.

proSelections.proposition: Christian belief centers on the historical Jesus and a self-sacrificing God whose cross motivates loving relationship rather than fearful appeasement.

conSelections.proposition: Scripture, souls, and an afterlife provide no sound basis for God because biblical narratives are largely unhistorical and mind-body dualism lacks support.
Personal religious experiences are psychologically unreliable and cannot establish religious truth without objective verification.
